label: GO step late in the episode (episode clock), earlier onset after an unrewarded trial
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (100% of activation mass; ~0 on D1/D2). Silent for the first ~55 trials of an episode, then the rate at GO rises steeply with episode trial (2% of GO steps in trials 60-69, 13% in 70-79, 27% in 80-89, 63% in 90-99, which hold 69% of the mass). It acts like an episode clock or end-of-episode signal. Consistently, it fires on low value-head output (value < 5.2 holds 72% of mass; nothing above 7.5), because value falls as the episode ends. Onset comes earlier when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward 0: rate 1.3x vs 0.8x after reward), and it fires on 86% of the rare steps with a penalty input. It is somewhat stronger when the policy prefers a2 (strongly negative choice logit), a mild effect not captured here. It is NOT tied to the core-trial pattern, transition, stay/switch, or the hidden good state. The simple version (phase == GO) & (ep_trial >= 80) gives dev F1 0.57 / mass recall 0.92. The recorded clause adding earlier onset after no reward gives dev F1 0.63 / mass recall 0.91. Precision stays limited because activation is graded with time and only crosses threshold on some late GO steps. Uses only observed or internal variables, no future ones.
